name: Nirupama Sanjeev
bio:
Career Overview: Nirupama Sanjeev (née Vaidyanathan) is a retired Indian tennis pioneer, notable for being the first Indian woman to win a Grand Slam main-draw match, retiring in 2010 after a comeback.

Playing Style: Known for her steady baseline game and tactical intelligence, she performed well on hard courts and clay.

Career-High WTA Singles Ranking: #147 (May 18, 1998)
Career-High WTA Doubles Ranking: #115 (July 24, 2000)

Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the second round of the Australian Open in 1998, defeating Miho Saeki.

Notable Achievements:
  • First Indian woman to win a Grand Slam main-draw match (1998 Australian Open).
  • Won 2 ITF singles titles and 5 ITF doubles titles.
  • Earned a bronze medal in mixed doubles at the 2006 Asian Games with Leander Paes.

Other Highlights:
  • Returned from retirement in 2010 to compete in the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games, reaching the doubles quarterfinals.
  • Paved the way for future Indian female players as the second woman after Nirupama Mankad to play professionally.

Nirupama’s groundbreaking career left a lasting impact on Indian tennis. 🎾🇮🇳
